source.title: Do LLMs "Feel"? Emotion Circuits Discovery and Control
source.authors: Chen-Xi Wang; Yixuan Zhang; Rui Yu; Yufei Zheng; Lang Gao; Zirui Song; Zi-Xiang Xu; Gus G. Xia; Hui-Shuai Zhang; Dongyan Zhao; Xiu-Ying Chen

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study analyzes emotion-related neurons and their causal effects, but it does not test the claim’s neuron-pole job counts, explanation fidelity on held-out activations, or the specific attribution-graph claim.
record.gate_note: The study reports neuron ablation and enhancement results, including Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct tables, that bear on neurons as localized emotion-related components. It does not count poles by number of understandable jobs or test explanations against new activations. Its emotion-generation accuracy, emotion-direction results, and attention-head results do not measure any listed claim version. Cited prior studies are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The study finds and steers emotion-related MLP neurons and attention heads in LLaMA-3.2-3B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. It measures how ablation or injection changes emotion-direction projection scores and emotion-expression accuracy. It never audits how many jobs neurons have, never scores neuron explanations against held-out activations, never examines vision neurons or superposition, and never builds attribution graphs with reconstruction error. None of its results bear on V1–V7. It does not cite the original sources either, so 'discusses' is the loosest fit: it treats neurons as meaningful causal units without addressing the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that emotion expression in LLMs comes from structured, context-agnostic emotion directions carried by a few neurons and attention heads. Integrated across layers, these form emotion circuits. Modulating the circuits without prompting gives 99.65% emotion-expression accuracy on the LLaMA test set, beating prompting and steering. They report low neuron overlap across emotions (0.056) and moderate head overlap (0.454).
record.recipe_differences: The study derives emotion directions and identifies emotion-related MLP neurons through contribution scores, then intervenes on them; it does not audit neuron poles or test generated explanations against unseen activating examples.
record.method_sensitivity: The effects vary with the number k of intervened neurons; the authors describe sharp early changes followed by plateaus for ablation and enhancement.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating a few top-ranked MLP neurons per layer (k=2–4) sharply lowers emotion-direction projection scores, and injecting emotion-difference vectors into them raises the scores. Random-neuron controls change the scores only slightly. Examples: Qwen anger ablation at k=2 gives -100.30 versus random -0.27; anger enhancement gives 27.66 versus random 0.07.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Targeted interventions on a small set of contribution-ranked MLP neurons causally shift a model's emotion representation. This shows that emotion-relevant computation is localized in neurons. It does not show that individual neurons have a single interpretable job.

record.problems: The study centers on one 3B model, with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct as an additional model; reported neuron-pole job shares and held-out explanation-prediction accuracy are absent. Several main-model intervention values are shown graphically rather than numerically.
record.rows_left_out: Within the 60-row limit, omitted Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct MLP-table entries at other k values and for other random-control emotion/k combinations; Tables 4 and 5 report these separately. Also omitted Qwen attention-head intervention tables (Tables 6 and 7), which concern heads rather than neuron-job interpretability, and other emotion-generation measures.

untested.parts: No audit of neuron poles or job counts in Qwen3-32B or any model.
No neuron-job shares across models, scales, dense versus MoE designs, or trillion-parameter models. The 3B and 7B models appear only for emotion interventions.
No InceptionV1 or other vision-neuron analysis, and no test of recursive generalization versus superposition.
No comparison of architectures, regularization or tools, and no interpretable-neuron share.
Circuits are assembled from neurons and heads by contribution scores, but no attribution graph is built and no explanation of behaviour or reconstruction error is compared with a replacement model.
No neuron explanations from activating examples, and no test of prediction on new firing.
No simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: The study is irrelevant to the claim's versions. Caveats if the rows are reused elsewhere: (1) The random-control rows R53–R56 are wrongly tied to anger; the table gives one Random column. (2) In Table 7 the random head ablation on Qwen is not negligible (e.g. -128.53 at k=1, -357.83 at k=10), which undercuts the text's 'negligible' claim for heads. No version depends on this. (3) The Qwen steering baseline fails for negative emotions (<5%), and circuit steering at scale 2.0 averages 66.18%. So control generalizes less well to Qwen than the 99.65% LLaMA figure suggests.

versions.untested_parts: No audit of neuron poles, job counts, or the share not understood.

Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct is included for emotion-component interventions, but the study does not measure neuron-job shares or scaling across model sizes, dense/MoE architectures, or trillion-parameter models.
No InceptionV1 cat-and-car analysis or test of recursive generalization versus superposition.
No comparison of architecture, regularization, tools, or interpretable-neuron estimates for vision models.
The study builds and modulates emotion circuits, but does not test attribution graphs as explanations of model behavior or report replacement-model reconstruction error.
No test of whether explanations fit activating examples but fail to predict firing elsewhere.
No automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulated activations on new text.

rows.subject: LLaMA-3.2-3B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Zeroed top-ranked emotion-related MLP neurons at the last-token gated activation; swept k.

conditions.value: held-out test set; emotions analyzed across the study

rows.measure: Change in aggregated emotion-direction projection score, Δs
rows.value: figure only; text says Δs drops sharply at k=2 and k=4, then quickly plateaus as k increases by over 30×
rows.uncertainty: 95% confidence intervals shown in figure; values not stated
rows.note: The text describes the sweep result, but the values are presented only in the figure.

rows.subject: LLaMA-3.2-3B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Zeroed randomly selected MLP neurons as an ablation control; random results averaged over 10 seeds.
rows.measure: Change in aggregated emotion-direction projection score, Δs
rows.value: figure only; text says random interventions have negligible impact
rows.uncertainty: 95% confidence intervals shown in figure; values not stated
rows.note: Control result is described in text; numeric values are not stated.

rows.subject: LLaMA-3.2-3B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Injected emotion-difference vectors into top-ranked emotion-related MLP neurons at the last-token position; swept k.
rows.measure: Change in aggregated emotion-direction projection score, Δs
rows.value: figure only; text says Δs rises sharply for small k and quickly saturates
rows.uncertainty: 95% confidence intervals shown in figure; values not stated
rows.note: The study interprets this score change as emotional representation enhancement, not as a test of single-job interpretability.

rows.subject: LLaMA-3.2-3B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Injected emotion-difference vectors into randomly selected or lower-ranked units as controls.
rows.measure: Change in aggregated emotion-direction projection score, Δs
rows.value: figure only; text says random or lower-ranked units have negligible effects
rows.uncertainty: 95% confidence intervals shown in figure; values not stated
rows.note: The qualitative control outcome is stated in text.
